messages:
incident-bot: Pager -> infer-usw1 oncall: kubelet NotReady flapping across multiple nodes in inference-pool-usw1. 30% of replicas currently NotReady, autoscaler attempted evac. Observed spike in PodRestarts and pod OOMs. See dashboard: https://console.redwood.local/alerts/4441 :rotating_light:

devin_pager: Ack. I'm on it. pulling logs now.

maria_oncall: I'm joining — checking kubelet logs and node telemetry. Any immediate customer impact observed?

nick_runtime: Observed serving runtime crashes on affected pods: repeated messages like `runtime error: cudart: driver shutdown` and `OOMKilled` in container status. Also seeing `kubelet: skipping beat - lost heartbeat` in node logs.

ops_triage: TL;DR: Kubelet heartbeat jitter -> nodes flapping NotReady -> kube-proxy endpoints churn -> client 502s for inference routes. Some customers reported elevated latency and a few 5xxs in last 4m.

maria_oncall: Running quick kubectl dump for one host: 
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer-usw1
infer-node-12   NotReady   4d   v1.26.3   10.128.2.45   us-west1
infer-node-13   NotReady   90m  v1.26.3   10.128.2.46   us-west1
infer-node-14   Ready      6d   v1.26.3   10.128.2.47   us-west1
```
And kubelet journal tail: 
```
kernel: watchdog: gpu_reset: GPU 0: reset triggered
kubelet[...]: E1124 12:03:41.123] failed to read cgroup stats: write /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/...: invalid argument
containerd: oom kill: "redwood-serve" pid=2345 oom_score_adj=0
kubelet: skipping heartbeat: last heartbeat 12s behind threshold
```

devin_pager: Looks like a mix of GPU driver resets and memory pressure. Could be a kernel/GPU driver regression. Are all NotReady nodes reporting GPU driver errors?

nick_runtime: Yes, GPU resets on 12 & 13. Node 12 also shows increased kernel logs `sched: RT throttling` and repeated `nv_peer_mem` complaints.

ops_triage: Immediate mitigations we should consider: 1) cordon + drain the two NotReady nodes to trigger pod reschedule to healthy nodes (if capacity). 2) Route inference traffic away from infer-usw1 via smart routing (failover to infer-usw2). 3) Temporarily disable GPU scheduling on suspect nodes (mark as unschedulable). 4) If pods repeatedly OOM, fallback to CPU-quantized model variant for affected customers.

maria_oncall: Actioning (1) now: `kubectl cordon infer-node-12 && kubectl drain infer-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` — starting live drain, will monitor reschedule.

devin_pager: Doing traffic steering: flipping routing rule for high-volume customers to prefer us-west2. `routing-service api` returning in-progress. Expect reduced 95p latency in ~30s.

cs_lead: Heads-up: two paying customers (AcmeMaps, ShopFast) reported increased tail latency and one 5xx each. I'm preparing an outbound note if this widens.

nick_runtime: During drain, a pod crashed on reschedule with `ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` just before OOM. Posting pod log snippet: 
```
I1124 12:05:02.234] model_worker.cc: loading weights
E1124 12:05:03.001] gpu_utils.cc: failed kernel launch: invalid device pointer
E1124 12:05:03.002] runtime.cc: unhandled CUDA exception: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
containerd: starting container failed: exit code 137
```

maria_oncall: That looks like transient GPU driver state corruption. I'm going to tag nodes for hardware-team and start kernel/GPU driver rolling back if drain finishes.

ops_triage: For safety: enable automatic fallback policy so requests that time out in 1.2s get routed to cached responses or lower-cost model variant. Maria, can you confirm fallback toggle?

maria_oncall: Confirmed. Toggling fallback policy now via console.

devin_pager: Routing flip succeeded. Telemetry: error rate down ~40% for the routes we pushed. Overall cluster still showing endpoint churn but client-facing impact decreasing.

sre_bot: Alert auto-escalation threshold hit: >20% pod restarts across inference-pool-usw1 for 8m. Filing SEV2 and paging infra-hardware-team. Incident incident-4441 created: https://incident.redwood.local/INC-4441

maria_oncall: Escalating to hardware team and infra. I'll attach node logs and kernel traces. Nick, please capture `dmesg -T` and `nvidia-smi -q` from the affected nodes before we reprovision.

nick_runtime: Collecting now and uploading to artifact store. `dmesg` shows repeated `GPU fault: reason=PAGE_FAULT` entries. nv-smi shows driver 525.85.12, CUDA 11.8.

ops_triage: Decision log: 1) Declare SEV2 (customer-impacting, partial degradation). 2) Route critical traffic to us-west2. 3) Continue drains; if pods fail to come up on new nodes, we will reprovision node image with older GPU driver and coordinate maintenance. 4) CS to send preliminary message to affected customers (AcmeMaps & ShopFast).

cs_lead: Draft outbound: "We are investigating increased latency/5xxs in us-west1. We've routed traffic to a healthy region and are actively remediating. We'll update in 30 minutes or earlier." OK to send?

maria_oncall: Send it. Add that we have no evidence of data loss and that mitigation is in progress.

devin_pager: Monitoring reschedules — new pods landing in infer-node-14 and in us-west2. CPU fallback path is accepting traffic for long requests now. Error rate trending down.

nick_runtime: Hardware team note: possible driver regression in 525.x series combined with high memory utilization on long-sequence requests. Recommend rolling nodes to driver 515.x as intermediate test if recoveries fail.

maria_oncall: If reschedules are healthy and error rate continues to drop we'll keep SEV2 and watch for 1h. If restarts continue, plan: reprovision image with 515 driver, mark old nodes for deeper hardware diagnostics.

ops_triage: Adding incident timeline and runbook to INC-4441. Please annotate any key commands you ran.

devin_pager: Noting `kubectl drain infer-node-12` and routing flip.

nick_runtime: Noting `systemd-run --scope -- dmesg -T > /artifacts/dmesg-node12.txt` and `nvidia-smi -q > /artifacts/nvsmi-node12.txt`.

sre_bot: Update: error rate 95p latency improved by 28%, request failures down 45%. Continuing monitoring.

maria_oncall: I'll leave cordon in place for infer-node-12/13 until hardware confirms. Keeping this thread active. If anyone sees a regression please ping @maria_oncall and @devin_pager.

cs_lead: Sent customer note. AcmeMaps acknowledged and appreciates the proactive routing.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4441 status: SEV2 active. Pager escalation to hardware-team and infra-team sent.

maria_oncall: 12:40 update: metrics stable, no new OOMs for 10m, keeping incident open for watch. Preparing postmortem draft once stabilized.

devin_pager: Thanks all. I'll hand off to morning oncall in 30m with context.
